title: Three-Program Recovery
subtitle: Autonomous Tournament, LIVEWELL, and RUNWELL—from recovery plan to reliable release.

projects.name: Autonomous Tournament
projects.outcome: Deliver a reliable Lessons Learned executive demonstration, contextual presentation, and credible extension opportunity. Demonstrate authenticated access, persisted results, an AI Core runtime, focused tests, and a deterministic fallback.
projects.current: Assessment: 30 August 2026. The assistant experience and Lessons Learned workflow exist. Remaining work centers on integrated authentication, deployed AI runtime, repeatability, and the executive narrative. Historical demo readiness estimate: 75–85%; not verified completion.
deferred: Runtime MCP extension until core demo is stable
phases: Development Setup: Kiro, SAP Proxy and CAP MCP

cost.adoptionDecision: Kiro intended; refine setup from real work

projects.name: LIVEWELL
projects.outcome: Build Ian’s personal early-warning system to identify potential NADEX trades for his review. Preserve the existing NADEX workflow and evaluate congressional disclosures as an additional contextual signal. Provide timely candidate alerts, clear reasons, and reproducible results so Ian can decide whether to trade.
projects.current: Assessment: 30 August 2026. A decision-support UI, data pipeline foundation, and backtesting framework exist. Source acquisition, lineage, asset mapping, and incremental-value validation remain. Historical readiness estimate: 60–70%; not verified completion.
deferred: Standalone trade triggers from congressional activity
Offering LIVEWELL to other users or as a commercial product
Central model gateway before a demonstrated need
phases: Development Setup: Kiro and AWS MCP

cost.adoptionDecision: Kiro intended; refine setup from real work

projects.name: RUNWELL
projects.outcome: Enable a design partner to run real fleet work: secure onboarding, recurring checklists, mobile execution, issues and service orders, with reliable deployment and support. Establish a practical path to paid use.
projects.current: Assessment: 30 August 2026. Broad SaaS and Business OS capabilities exist. Delivery confidence depends on green CI, tenant isolation, a reproducible deployment, and a verified charter workflow. Historical readiness estimate: 50–60%; not verified completion.
phases: Development Setup: Kiro and AWS MCP

cost.adoptionDecision: Kiro intended; refine setup from real work

tasks.title: Install gstack for Kiro from Ian’s fork
tasks.description:
One-time machine setup. If ~/gstack is absent, run:
git clone --single-branch --depth 1 https://github.com/ianfmc/gstack.git ~/gstack
cd ~/gstack
./setup --host kiro

If the directory exists, check its origin and local changes before updating; do not clone over it. Review the setup script first. Setup builds the browser tools and installs Chromium when needed. Keep the source checkout in place because installed runtime assets link to it. Record the actual commit with git -C ~/gstack rev-parse HEAD. The reviewed reference is e23ff280a1c2e517daaee89ccc1a0e415e5aa9bc. Use the explicit Kiro host; the default and Claude team/local instructions are not the Kiro installation route.
tasks.phase: Development Setup: Kiro, SAP Proxy and CAP MCP
acceptanceCriteria: Kiro skill files and runtime assets resolve in this project’s environment.
Installation succeeds without the missing generated-skills warning; investigate bun run build and rerun setup if that warning occurs.

tasks.title: Confirm gstack skill discovery in this Kiro workspace
tasks.description: Open only this project in Kiro and start a fresh agent session after setup. Inspect Agent Steering & Skills and the slash-command menu for the installed gstack review and browser skills. Invoke the names actually exposed by this installation. If using a custom CLI agent, verify its resources include skill://~/.kiro/skills/*/SKILL.md. Check for workspace skills that shadow the global names; do not copy the root repository as a standalone skill and lose its runtime dependencies.
tasks.phase: Development Setup: Kiro, SAP Proxy and CAP MCP
acceptanceCriteria: Kiro discovers and loads the installed review and browser skill instructions.
The selected agent can locate the browser runtime; record any IDE/CLI-specific limitation.
